clue.text: One drawing on film without restriction on series

parts.note: a U certificate marks a film open to all, with no age restriction

explanation.surface: A cinema-goer binges a whole series with no limit on viewing.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film classification 'Universal', suitable for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who draws on a resource, such as a supply or service, consumes it.

clue.text: Urban one in common TV programme about north

indicators.note: the TV programme's letters are placed around the abbreviation for north

parts.note: TOWIE, The Only Way Is Essex, a British reality show often mocked as vulgar or common
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A city dweller appears in a lowbrow television show set up north.
explanation.walkthrough: TOWIE is The Only Way Is Essex, a British reality series; 'common' is the snobbish British word for vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: A city person, as opposed to someone from the countryside, is an informal synonym.

clue.text: See 13 across
A number in group function

indicators.note: the article and the number's abbreviation are put inside the word for group

parts.note: a sect is a group of followers

explanation.surface: A figure belonging to a set is plugged into a mathematical function.
explanation.definitionFit: A trigonometric function, the reciprocal of cosine, so an example of a mathematical function.

clue.text: See 13 across
Box blows up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for blows is read from bottom to top

parts.note: raps are sharp blows or knocks

explanation.surface: A boxing match where the punches escalate.
explanation.definitionFit: To box lightly in practice is a synonym; boxers do this in training.

clue.text: Sister on time after second part of film's overrun

indicators.note: the nun and date come after the letter taken from film
in a down clue, the sister sits on top of the time
picks the second letter of the word film

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: A film runs over schedule; a nun is late to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood or swamp something is to overrun it, as with too many applications.

clue.text: Works parts of a drama

definitions.meaning: a play is divided into these major sections

explanation.definitionFit: Deeds are actions or works; a play is also split into large divisions with this name.

clue.text: Unable to catch director — fade out

parts.note: Oliver Stone, the film director

indicators.note: the letters of fade are put out of order

explanation.surface: A film direction: the shot of the director fades out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unable to catch' means unable to hear anything, not unable to grab.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely deaf: someone so afflicted cannot catch a word that is said.

clue.text: Slate one on Cape Fear

parts.note: to pan a film is to slate it in a review
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A critic slates a remake of Cape Fear, the Scorsese thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden overwhelming fright or alarm is the sense shared here.

clue.text: Hastily produced and directed Pixar film

parts.note: to run an operation is to direct it
Up is a 2009 Pixar animated film

explanation.surface: Someone rushed out and directed an animated Pixar picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something up is to make it quickly, as with a dress run up overnight.

clue.text: They follow workers entertaining director in this place

indicators.note: the workers hold the director and the place inside, as a host entertains guests

parts.note: worker ants, so ants are crossword workers
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Film crew members host their director on location.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters or followers of a cause or person are said to be people who follow.

clue.text: Harry Potter film attaches this: not for film

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so the following words are disrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which Harry Potter film adds a scene, saying it is not suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry Potter film' reads as one unit, but Harry is the anagram signal; the fodder is 'Potter film attaches this' plus 'not'. The second 'film' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese's 1988 picture about Jesus, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Listen in to TV show one records

parts.note: to tap a phone line is to listen in
ER is the American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: Someone eavesdrops on a television programme while recording it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who records on tape, a crossword-style sense of someone who makes recordings.

clue.text: Satellite delayed, screening start of Shutter Island

indicators.note: the moon's name hides the first letter within it, as a screen covers something

parts.note: Io is a moon of Jupiter

indicators.note: takes the first letter of Shutter

parts.note: late means delayed

explanation.surface: A satellite broadcast of Shutter Island, Scorsese's thriller, is late in starting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island' is a verb here: to cut off, as the sea cuts off an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To island someone is to set them apart, cutting them off from others entirely.

clue.text: Gave away too much space? Left love to give approval in bed

parts.note: over means left, as in leftover

indicators.note: the love and approval go inside the word for bed

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis
OK means to approve

explanation.surface: A tale of leftover love and approval given in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels or airlines that sell more places than they hold have promised too much room.

clue.text: Turning over English TV channel for escape

indicators.note: the English abbreviation and the channel are read backwards, turned the other way

parts.note: Dave is a British TV channel

explanation.surface: Flicking channels to an English TV station to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Dave is a British comedy and entertainment TV channel.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude or dodge, avoiding something by cleverness, is the verb sense of escape.

clue.text: Italian artist in Italy after Hollywood actor

indicators.note: the abbreviation for Italy comes after the actor

parts.note: Sean Penn, the Hollywood actor
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An Italian painter follows a Hollywood star in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gianfrancesco Penni was a Renaissance painter, an assistant of Raphael.

clue.text: Initially going in, son's seen Raging Bull

indicators.note: raging means wild, so the letters are thrown about
the first letter of the word in goes, leaving its last

parts.note: son, with the 's read as has

explanation.surface: A son watches Raging Bull, Scorsese's boxing film, starting to go in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially going' removes the I from 'in', leaving N, which joins SON and SEEN to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Bull is slang for rubbish or claptrap, empty talk not worth hearing.

clue.text: Second film shot here?

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film

explanation.surface: Asking where a sequel was shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A film set is the stage or location where scenes are shot.

clue.text: Film man processes topless shot

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are rearranged
the first letter of processes is removed, like a head cut off

explanation.surface: A film man develops a topless shot in the darkroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is the director, the film man behind all this puzzle's titles.

clue.text: Characters in scene making medical treatment

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words scene making

explanation.surface: Actors in a hospital scene administer a treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure that flushes the bowel with fluid is a medical treatment.

clue.text: To quarrel before hit

indicators.note: the word for quarrel comes before To

parts.note: a run-in is an argument or quarrel
taken as written

explanation.surface: Arguing first, then throwing a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: To collide with something, as a car striking a wall, is to hit it.

clue.text: Green taxi driver's short days

indicators.note: the last letter of the driver's name is dropped

parts.note: a cabby drives a taxi
an age, as in 'in his day', is a period of time

explanation.surface: Taxi Driver, Scorsese's film, as a green taxi driver's short days.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy vegetable is one of the greens; also slang for money.

clue.text: Film about crime ring

parts.note: ca. is circa, meaning about
a sin is a wrongdoing
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A film about a crime ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorsese's 1995 gangster picture set in Las Vegas, so an example of a film.

clue.text: Each star hugs tart

indicators.note: the word for star wraps around the word for tart

parts.note: an ace is a star performer
a pie or tart is a pastry

explanation.surface: A celebrity embraces a woman described rudely.
explanation.definitionFit: Per item, for every one, as in 'a pound per item' — a synonym.

clue.text: Hot stuff within these threesomes, having stolen one tablet to perform?

indicators.note: the remaining letters perform, acting out a new order
the tablet is taken out of the word threesomes

parts.note: E is ecstasy, a single pill

explanation.surface: A racy scene of threesomes and stolen pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot stuff' suggests something sexy but means hot drinks held in flasks.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacuum flasks keep drinks warm, so hot liquids sit inside them.

clue.text: Gather food

definitions.meaning: British slang for food, especially sweets at school

explanation.definitionFit: A fold sewn into cloth gathers it; schoolboy slang also uses it for snacks.

clue.text: Film not heard by audience …

indicators.note: what an audience hears, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: a sound that is missed is not heard

explanation.surface: A film unheard by its audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin layer or haze, such as condensation, is a film.

clue.text: Oscar parts for The Departed scripts?

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO alphabet
bits are parts

explanation.surface: Oscar-winning roles in the Scorsese film The Departed.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title becomes 'the departed', the dead, whose scripts are obituaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Death notices are written pieces about those who have died.

clue.text: … while in quiet frame

indicators.note: the word for while goes inside the word for quiet

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
as means while

explanation.surface: Continuing the film thread: staying quiet within the frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The frame of a window holding the glass is called a window frame.

clue.text: Gives parts to son in show

indicators.note: the son's abbreviation goes inside the show

parts.note: Cats is the stage musical

explanation.surface: A director gives roles to his son in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate roles in a play or film to actors is to assign parts.

clue.text: Decisions of 10 cutting bad scenes

indicators.note: the number cuts into the middle of the scrambled scenes
the letters of scenes are bad, put in wrong order

parts.note: ten is written as a word

explanation.surface: Editing decisions: ten bad scenes get cut.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10 across, but it simply gives TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Judicial rulings on punishment are judges' decisions in court.
